title: Cache telemetry data quality QA checklist (prefix/KV cache)
body:
Purpose
This is the QA checklist we run before (a) enabling new cache telemetry flags in production and (b) trusting cache metrics as inputs to dashboards/alerts/recommendations.

Scope
- Ingestion/data quality for cache telemetry: missing tags, counter resets, histogram bucket sanity, cross-region consistency, ingestion drops, and joinability with gateway/model context.
- Applies to: Hosted API, Dedicated, Private (where supported), across regions.
- Non-goals: correctness of cache algorithm itself (covered by runtime integration tests + perf canary), and UI/Console correctness.

Owners / review
- Primary: Allison Grant (SRE Observability)
- Ingestion/cardinality: Caleb Johnson
- Pipeline/aggregation: Thomas Baird
- Metrics schema: Nadia Rahman
- Telemetry pipelines: Logan Wright
- QA automation: Leila Farouk

Pre-reqs / where to look
- Dashboards: “Cache hit-rate overview” + “Cache telemetry ingestion health” (observability-pack)
- Runtime flags: see runtime release notes + config flags (pr-18429)
- Naming/cardinality policy: Confluence (observability standards) — make sure we’re using the renamed metrics (pr-18431) and that old names are not powering new dashboards.
- Known tricky semantics:
  - streaming retries (fixed in pr-18428)
  - continuous batching prefill hit attribution (fixed in pr-18433)

Checklist A — Basic ingestion sanity (are we receiving data?)
A1. Metric presence
- Confirm the expected metric families exist in the metrics backend for each environment (staging, canary, prod).
- If a metric is missing entirely:
  - verify runtime flag enabled for that env
  - verify ingestion allowlist isn’t dropping the metric name
  - verify exporter is running on all runtime pods

A2. Freshness / last-seen
- For each region, check “last seen timestamp” panels for cache metrics.
- Expected: data points continue arriving at normal cadence; no gaps > 2x scrape interval (or > 5m in aggregated pipelines).
- Red flags:
  - gaps in a single region only (regional pipeline issue)
  - gaps for only one deployment mode (tagging/allowlist mismatch)

A3. Drop counters / ingestion errors
- Check ingestion service logs/metrics for:
  - label-drop counts
  - series reject counts
  - rate-limit triggers
- Expected: some label-drop can be normal if clients send forbidden labels, but the rate should be stable and low; any step-change after rollout is a gating issue.

Checklist B — Required tag coverage (missing tags)
Goal: ensure we can slice by Redwood operational dimensions without exploding cardinality.

B1. Required tags present (coverage)
For cache metrics, validate presence of required tags (as per standards policy). At minimum we expect:
- model (or model_family) + model_version_id (where allowed)
- route_id (allowlisted / canonical)
- deployment_mode (hosted|dedicated|private)
- region
- prompt_length_bucket (or request_shape_bucket) on reuse histograms
- miss_reason on miss breakdown metrics (where applicable)

Procedure
- Pick 3 representative regions (us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1) and 2 models (one chat, one instruct).
- For each, query tag coverage rate:
  - % of samples with each required tag
  - % of samples with tag=unknown / tag=unset (depending on implementation)

Expected
- region + deployment_mode should be effectively 100%
- model family should be near-100% once request context propagation is live
- route_id may be <100% during migration windows, but should not exceed the rollout gate threshold agreed in go/no-go (ask Ethan Park if unsure).

Red flags
- sudden increase in “unknown” tags after deployment
- a single tag missing across all metrics (likely gateway-to-runtime context regression)
- route_id missing only on one deployment mode (Dedicated/Private tag propagation divergence)

B2. Tag value allowlist sanity
- Verify route_id/model_version_id values match the allowlists used by ingestion guards.
- Check for patterns indicating raw/unbounded strings leaking:
  - UUIDs not in allowlist
  - route names including tenant/user identifiers
  - model_version_id mismatching control-plane format

If found
- Treat as P0 privacy/cardinality risk. Roll back telemetry enablement and/or tighten ingestion drop rules; file ticket to Platform Tagging (Ethan Park / Amara Diallo).

Checklist C — Cardinality budget guardrails (series explosion detection)
C1. Series counts by metric
- For each cache metric family, compare current series count vs expected budget.
- Expected: series growth roughly proportional to (regions * allowlisted routes * models * prompt buckets), not proportional to tenants/users.

C2. Top label combinations
- Identify top-N label combinations by sample volume and by unique series.
- Ensure “tenant_id” (or equivalents) are not present. If present at all, ingestion should drop it.

C3. Sampling behavior sanity
- Confirm sampling labels (if any) are stable and not creating additional dimensions.
- Confirm sampling rate doesn’t flip dynamically per pod in a way that makes aggregates unusable.

Checklist D — Counter correctness (resets / monotonicity / double counting)
D1. Counter resets
- For counters (hits, misses, evictions, wasted_prefill_tokens), compute reset rate per pod.
- Expected: resets only on pod restart/rollout. A rolling deploy will show some resets; a stable cluster should show near-zero resets.
- Red flags:
  - frequent resets without deploys (crash loops)
  - resets aligned with scrape interval (exporter bug)

D2. Negative rates / impossible deltas
- Check rate() on counters for negative spikes.
- Negative spikes usually indicate:
  - resets not handled in query
  - duplicate timeseries identity collisions (label instability)

D3. Streaming retries double counting regression check
- Re-run the known reproduction for streaming retries (from runtime notes) and verify:
  - hit/miss counters do not inflate beyond expected request count
  - retry attempts do not create additional “phantom” cache events
- If seen, verify pr-18428 is in the runtime version deployed.

D4. Batched prefill attribution sanity
- For a continuous batching workload, validate that:
  - total hits + misses aligns with request count (within expected sampling error)
  - per-request histograms don’t show impossible reuse depths
- If off, verify pr-18433 is in the runtime version deployed.

Checklist E — Histogram bucket sanity (prompt length, reuse depth, token counts)
E1. Bucket boundaries match spec
- Verify bucket edges (prompt length buckets, reuse depth, token hist bins) match the published standards.
- Red flag: non-standard buckets (e.g., 513, 1025 edges) indicating code drift.

E2. Sum-of-buckets ~= count
- For each histogram metric:
  - sum(rate(bucket)) should approximate rate(count)
- Allow small drift due to scrape timing; large drift suggests exporter bug or ingestion truncation.

E3. No “all in +Inf” symptom
- If most samples land in +Inf bucket:
  - bucket edges too small
  - units mismatch (tokens vs bytes)
  - wrong field mapped

E4. No empty interior buckets (unless workload-specific)
- Completely empty interior buckets across all regions/models is suspicious.
- Validate with at least two distinct request shapes:
  - short prompts (<=256 tokens)
  - long prompts (>=2k tokens)

Checklist F — Cross-region consistency & comparability
F1. Consistent tag vocab across regions
- Ensure region names are normalized (e.g., us-east-1 not useast1).
- Ensure deployment_mode vocabulary is consistent across regions.

F2. Comparable baseline ranges
- Compare hit-rate and wasted prefill across regions for the same model + route under similar traffic.
- Expected: differences exist (locality, routing), but should not be wildly divergent without a routing/traffic explanation.

F3. Detect “silent drop” in one region
- Use a cross-region panel that shows:
  - request volume proxy (e.g., total decode tokens)
  - cache metric volume
- If request proxy stays steady but cache metrics drop to near-zero in one region, suspect ingestion drop or tagging mismatch.

Checklist G — Joinability checks (gateway/control-plane ↔ runtime metrics)
G1. Model version consistency
- Pick a model rollout window (canary → prod).
- Validate model_version_id observed in runtime metrics matches the control-plane version id shown in gateway logs/analytics.
- Red flag: “version_mismatch” miss_reason spikes after rollout (also seen in SUP-3912 type incidents).

G2. Route identifier migration
- Validate route_id used in runtime metrics matches route_id used in gateway metrics.
- During migration, ensure we have either:
  - dual-write (old+new) with controlled duration, or
  - stable mapping layer.

G3. Private/Dedicated isolation
- For Dedicated, ensure customer identifiers are NOT present as metric labels.
- For slicing, rely on allowlisted “dedicated_pool_id” or similar coarse identifiers if approved; otherwise aggregate by deployment_mode only.

Checklist H — Privacy checks (must-pass)
H1. No raw prompts
- Confirm no metric label contains:
  - prompt text
  - user message text
  - tool inputs
- Confirm any hash/canonicalization identifiers are either (a) not emitted as labels, or (b) coarse-bucketed and allowlisted.

H2. No user identifiers
- Confirm labels do not contain:
  - end_user_id
  - email
  - IP
  - session ids

If violation suspected
- Stop rollout and page Security/Privacy review owner (Marcus Lin) + SRE oncall.

Checklist I — Alert/dashboard readiness (data quality gates)
I1. Dashboard panels not blank / not misleading
- Validate key panels render for:
  - prod total
  - per region
  - per model family
  - per deployment mode
- Validate panels behave under low-traffic scenarios (don’t show 0% hit-rate due to no samples; should show N/A or hide).

I2. Alert gating uses traffic-aware logic
- For cache-efficiency guardrails, confirm alerts have:
  - minimum traffic threshold
  - rate-of-change logic where applicable
  - suppression during known rollout windows

I3. “Telemetry missing” vs “real regression” split
- Ensure we have a separate alert or dashboard indicator for:
  - ingestion drop
  - series reject spikes
  - scrape failures
So we don’t page on a fake hit-rate dip.

Acceptance criteria (rollout go/no-go)
Must-pass:
- Required tag coverage within thresholds agreed for the rollout stage (staging/canary/prod)
- No evidence of raw prompt/user identifiers in labels
- Series counts within budget (no step-change trend)
- No systematic counter double counting (stream retries, batched prefill)
- Histogram buckets match spec and look plausible
- Cross-region views do not show “silent drop” in a subset of regions

Nice-to-have (can follow up with ticket):
- Minor route_id coverage gaps during migration
- Small bucket distribution anomalies explainable by workload mix

Common failure modes (notes from prior rollouts)
- Label-drop misconfig causes dashboards to show zero hits (see customer-facing symptom: SUP-3927 pattern).
- Route tagging rolled out in gateway but not propagated into runtime metrics (joinability breaks).
- Metric rename shipped but dashboards still query old names (post pr-18431 cleanup required).
- Sampling changes create sudden apparent hit-rate change (denominator mismatch).

Runbook pointers
If anything fails this checklist:
- For ingestion drops/label rejects: follow “cache telemetry pipeline incident runbook” (Confluence) and loop in Caleb Johnson + Logan Wright.
- For runtime counter/hist correctness: loop in Omar El-Sayed + Samir Qureshi; confirm deployed runtime version includes pr-18428/pr-18433 fixes.

Change log
- 2025-03-07: Initial checklist drafted (Allison)
- 2025-03-10: Added streaming retry + batched prefill regression checks; added privacy must-pass section (Caleb/Leila feedback)
- 2025-03-12: Updated joinability section to call out model_version mismatch incidents + route migration gotchas (Logan/Nadia feedback)
